title: Chapter 11 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of physics, collisions, triggers, and materials!

questions.question: What two components are needed for a dynamic physics object?
questions.explanation: Collider defines shape; Rigidbody enables physics.

questions.question: What makes a collider static (non‑moving) to the physics engine?
options: It has a Rigidbody with Is Kinematic = true
It is marked 'Static' in the Inspector
questions.explanation: Without a Rigidbody, the collider is considered static.

questions.question: How can you change gravity at runtime?
options: Change the Gravity setting in the Rigidbody
questions.explanation: Physics.gravity is a global static variable.

questions.question: What does the Drag property on a Rigidbody do?
options: Reduces linear velocity over time (air resistance)
questions.explanation: Drag simulates air resistance, slowing the object.

questions.question: Which ForceMode applies an instant velocity change ignoring mass?
questions.explanation: VelocityChange directly sets velocity without mass influence.

questions.question: When would you set a Rigidbody to Is Kinematic?
options: When it should fall under gravity
When you want to move it only by script and not be affected by forces
When you want it to bounce
questions.explanation: Kinematic objects ignore physics forces but can be moved via transform or MovePosition.

questions.question: Interpolation on a Rigidbody smooths the object's visual movement between physics steps.
questions.explanation: Interpolation helps reduce jitter for fast-moving Rigidbodies.

questions.question: Which collision detection mode prevents fast objects from tunneling through walls?
questions.explanation: Continuous and Continuous Dynamic sweep the object's path to detect collisions.

questions.question: Which collider type is most suitable for a humanoid character?
questions.explanation: Capsule Colliders handle slopes and movement well.

questions.question: What does the 'Is Trigger' checkbox do on a Collider?
options: Converts it into a sensor that only fires trigger events
questions.explanation: A trigger collider detects overlaps without physical collision.

questions.question: Which method is called when a Rigidbody enters a trigger collider?
questions.explanation: OnTriggerEnter is the standard trigger event.

questions.question: What does the Collision parameter in OnCollisionEnter provide?
options: The name of the other object
Detailed info like contact points, impulse, and the other GameObject
questions.explanation: Collision holds contacts, relative velocity, and the other object's info.

questions.question: Why is `other.CompareTag("Player")` preferred over `other.tag == "Player"`?
options: It's faster and generates less garbage
questions.explanation: CompareTag is more efficient and avoids string allocation.

questions.question: What is a Physics Material used for?
options: To change the color of a collider
To define bounciness and friction for a collider
questions.explanation: Physics Materials control surface properties like friction and bounce.

questions.question: What does a Bounciness value of 0 mean?
questions.explanation: 0 bounciness means inelastic collision (no rebound).

questions.question: How do you combine friction from two colliders?
options: Using the Friction Combine mode (Average, Min, Max, Multiply)
Only the first object's friction is used
questions.explanation: The Physics Material's Combine setting determines how two surfaces' properties merge.

questions.question: Which joint is best for a door that swings open?
questions.explanation: Hinge Joint rotates around one axis.

questions.question: What is required for a collision or trigger event to fire?
options: At least one must have a Rigidbody
questions.explanation: At least one of the interacting objects needs a Rigidbody.

questions.question: You can use a 3D Physics Material on a 2D collider.
questions.explanation: 3D Physics Materials work only with 3D colliders; 2D has its own Physics Material 2D.

questions.question: How do you prevent a player Rigidbody from tipping over?
options: Freeze rotation constraints on X and Z
questions.explanation: Freezing rotation prevents unwanted tilting.

questions.question: What is a compound collider?
options: Multiple colliders on the same GameObject approximating a complex shape
A collider that works with joints
questions.explanation: Using several primitive colliders together gives a better approximation without the cost of a Mesh Collider.

questions.question: When using OnTriggerStay, how often is it called?
questions.explanation: Like other physics callbacks, OnTriggerStay is called per fixed update.

questions.question: What could cause OnCollisionEnter to not fire even when objects visually touch?
options: One object has a Rigidbody but is sleeping
The layers are set to ignore each other in the collision matrix
questions.explanation: Sleeping objects may not fire; layer matrix can disable interactions; triggers fire trigger events, not collisions.

questions.question: You can change a Collider's size at runtime via script.
questions.explanation: The size, center, and other properties of colliders can be modified in code.
